newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma seeks alternative to big spending cuts.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma seeks alternative to big spending cuts.

text.p: The budget committee of the lower house of Russia's parliament asked the government on Thursday to withdraw its draconian plan to cut spending by over 100 trillion roubles ($17.4 billion), and said deputies should consider alternative ideas.

Itar-Tass news agency quoted Duma deputies as saying that the chamber, which is dominated by communists and other conservatives, should consider an alternative plan put forward by a group of deputies when it debates the issue on Friday.

It was not clear what alternatives the budget committee was talking about, but many deputies are attracted by the idea of doubling money supply, viewing it as a way to pay off wage arrears and ease the financial pains of the population.
Ministers and central bank officials said boosting the money supply would only rekindle inflation and have rejected the idea.
A Duma vote would not be binding on the government.

Ministers, taking comfort from vague phrasing in the budget law -- which says the government must submit new spending plans to parliament but does not say that parliament must approve the plans -- are likely to ignore the Duma.

The government, worried that dismal tax revenues have made a mockery of figures underpinning the 1997 budget, has already ordered ministries to cut spending and is telling ministries not to order goods which they cannot afford to pay for.
It wants the Duma to approve its decision to slash over 100 trillion roubles, effectively approving a new "realistic" budget. Deputies are likely to vote on the issue on Friday.
